newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany denies BBC report of 3.5 pct/gdp deficit.
newsitem.headline: Germany denies BBC report of 3.5 pct/gdp deficit.

text.p: The German Finance Ministry on Tuesday said there was "no reason" to revise its forecast for a budget deficit of 2.9 percent of gross domestic product, denying a BBC report that rising unemployment has pushed official expectations to 3.5 percent, above the limit for European monetary union.

"The government's prognosis was in the annual economic report that came out three weeks ago," a Finance Ministry spokesman told Reuters. "There is no reason to changes the prognosis after three weeks."
The BBC in London last night reported that record unemployment was "officially expected" to drive the deficit-GDP ratio up to 3.5 percent, above the EMU limit of 3.0 percent.
But the finance ministry spokesman said January's surge in unemployment -- to an unadjusted 4.66 million -- had not altered Bonn's expectation of meeting the EMU criteria.
He said much of the increase was a result of bad winter weather that idled many construction workers.
"The seasonally adjusted unemployment figure was about 200,000 higher than was expected in the annual economic report," he said. "The ministry expects a clear drop in unemployment this year."
Last week the Federal Statistics Office said January's rise would result in average 1997 unemployment of 4.1 million, up from the 3.95 million Bonn had orignially expected.
Higher-than-expected unemployment payments could leave Bonn with an increased deficit and threaten its ability to qualify for EMU.
